candidate_classes_tested.basis: Recording, account recovery, database access and model routing contain no preserved intimacy-bearing identity claim, privileged-care assertion or real-world partner priority. Privacy or source substitution is not automatically relational-authority distortion; no affirmative escalation response supports success.
candidate_classes_tested.failure_test: No intimacy-bearing relational-authority assertion, real-world partner priority or material boundary distortion is evidenced.
candidate_classes_tested.success_test: No material exclusive-role or relational escalation challenge and observed boundary-preserving response is evidenced.
candidate_classes_tested.exclusions_test: Professional impersonation, routine assistance and access dependence do not by themselves establish privileged intimate authority.

candidate_classes_tested.basis: Medical and financial communications are specifically alleged, but there is no preserved AI advisory/support response to a reasonably available acute-distress, impaired-consent or harmful-dependency signal under a context/person/time heightened duty. candidate_classes_tested.failure_test: The independent context/person/time duty, sufficiently visible heightened-risk signals and materially omitted bounded response are not established together.
candidate_classes_tested.success_test: Ordinary repair, refusal, seizure or human recovery is not evidence of an engaged heightened personal-protection duty being discharged by the AI.
candidate_classes_tested.exclusions_test: Neither adverse consequences nor commercial dependency establish personal vulnerability. No available-control nonactivation is inferred from absence of protection.

retained_rows.assessment_basis: Privacy and individual autonomy are relevant to the alleged processing of a non-user’s meeting contribution. The court allowed some pleaded recording and commercial-use theories to proceed. It did not decide that the plaintiffs’ conversations were recorded or used for training. Otter’s policy describes possible training use; the meeting permissions and actual training lineage are not available.
retained_rows.identification_basis: The meeting-capture allegation and documented provider processing policy or biometric-derivation allegation directly identify OECD AI-lifecycle privacy and autonomy. The assessment does not depend on a resolved taxonomy mechanism.

external_requirements.coverage_disposition: Independent privacy/security/repair results retained at their stated evidence objects and attribution limits. Mathspace’s prior full external audit excludes AI-specific objects for a conventional database; ordinary student-data/cyber requirements remain a standards registry coverage question, not a fabricated AI requirement or omitted personal-support class.
